abstract: We develop global indicators for tracking how species assemblages respond to climate change by estimating community climate indices based on species maximum temperature and minimum aridity niche limits. We applied them to global databases using 33.6 million occurrence records from the past half-century to track assemblage changes for 26,163 species of terrestrial vertebrates. Changes in community climate indices tracked climate changes, weakening at higher elevations and strengthening at higher latitudes. Species that disappeared from sampled locations were intolerant of hot and dry conditions, while colonising species were characteristic of warmer and drier locales. Trends differed markedly within subcontinental regions, ecoregions and countries. Many vertebrate assemblages are responding to climate change yet lags in some regions and countries raise concerns that they are not keeping pace.
